utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We continue to be in closed session, the technicians tell me, yes. Mr. Niemann?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have spoken to the witness over the course of the night and I have reminded him of the contempt provisions of these Rules. I must say that it is not easy to threaten a person with six months imprisonment (redacted) (redacted) or with a $10,000 fine when they are penniless, but the witness tells me that his view of the matter is that he only has left his family and he has a duty to protect them. The way he sees it, that if in a struggle to protect his family the transcript of his evidence before this court has to be struck out, then he believes that the interests of his family come first. But, having discussed it with him, he is prepared, your Honour, to return to the box and to resume his testimony and to answer Mr. Kay's questions. For my part, I have promised him that I will be objecting to each and every question which is arguably in breach of the order. With respect to that, your Honour, and in relation to the matters raised by the Defence, it is our submission that anything that we may have discovered to the Defence in no way gives them licence to breach the order of the Court. That will be our position on that. Finally, your Honour, the witness has asked me to ask the Court for their indulgence to permit him to explain his position. He has promised me that he will be short in doing so, he will be respectful and polite to the Court, but he wants to explain why it is that he has taken this position, but he is prepared to return to the box and to answer the questions, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Niemann indicated these matters to me earlier and I guess we see how we proceed, your Honour. I am mindful of the Court's order.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. Then call the witness in and we will continue. He may explain. We have already advised him of the possibility of his being cited for contempt, considering that admonition, then he may respond if he wishes by way of an explanation, a brief explanation. WITNESS L, recalled.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Sir, you understand that you are still under the oath that you gave yesterday to tell the truth, do you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I understand that, from Mr. Niemann, you wish to respond to the position taken by the Trial Chamber yesterday, that questions that had been directed to you by Mr. Kay were in issue in this case and that you should respond to those questions subject to the possibility of being held in contempt. You may respond, if you wish.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I apologise for yesterday's reasons which I have not given to the Court the names and I apologise to the Defence. My problems are such that I have lost my father. I do not, I know that there is no one to protect my mother and my sisters. I have to do it myself, to protect my mother and my sisters, because I lost my father and because I worked at the camp, and I repent for everything that I have done in that camp that I should not have done, and I admit to having done it. Otherwise, I did not want to go on television or some camera or to the newspapers to give any evidence against Tadic involving my family.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Kay, would you like to continue with cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Cross-examined by MR. KAY, continued.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, yesterday you told the Court that your shift duty at Trnopolje camp was from 7.00 in the morning until 7.00 in the evening, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I would like you to tell me is the names of the other guards who were on that shift at the same time as you, and if you could give the names slowly so that we can hear them clearly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Zoran Ergarac, Julije Cindric, Sinisa Popovic, Sasa Popovic, Bosko Dragicevic, Zoran Karajica, Zeljko Karajica, Dragan Baltic, Dusko Tadic, Milan Cavic. Those are the ones that I can remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have told us that you were at guard post 4. How many guard posts were there around the camp at this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Four.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you with another guard or other guards at guard post 4?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The other three guard posts, did they have single guards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The duties of the guards who were not on guard post duty were what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as the guard duties are concerned, they were only that the civilians would not come out of the camp and that the military and other civilians, the locals, do not approach the camp and do not do to the people what they should not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a fence around the camp at this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a mesh wire and then there was barbed wire which was about 2 to 2.5 metres high.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we can look at that plan that you drew upon yesterday, D34, please, and if the overhead projector could be switched on and D34 placed on there? What I would like you to do is to indicate with the pointer where the fence that you have described extended around the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My guard post was here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The second one was behind the school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just keep the pointer there on the map so that we can see where the second guard post was. That is your guard post. The second guard post, you were just telling us, was where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The third guard post was, sorry, here where you see -- that was the fence, that line. Then there was a guard post No. 1 which was near the substation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Was that clear to the Court, the markings?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Clear. Do you want him to mark on your 34?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would, if possible.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, witness. If you could just mark then those other positions of guard posts on that plan that is on the overhead projector? Take it off the overhead projector and put the plan in front of you now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the plan].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whilst you have the plan there in front of you, you put it back on the projector, if you could just indicate with the marker where the two metre, two and a half metre fence stretched around the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The fence ran from the road going to the store, from my guard post up to guard post No. 3, from guard post No. 3 to straight to the road leading to Prijedor, to the guard post No. 2. From the guard post No. 2 along the road leading to Prijedor down to guard post No. 1, the electric substation. Then from the substation to the entrance to the dom and the store, that was the gate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could put the plan back in front of you now and with that red biro you have on your desk, if you could just draw around the map that route of the fence around the camp? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the plan].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, witness. If you could just put it back on the overhead projector and leave it there so that we can see it? Yes. Was this fence the same height all the way round the camp of two metres or two and a half metres?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the barbed wired on the top section of the fence or the bottom section?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On top of the fence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The wire below was what sort of wire, are you able to describe it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was like a mesh.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was your guard post inside the wire fence or on the outside of the wire fence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Inside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you were relieved from duty, that would have been one of the other guards coming from within the camp, would it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell me now the names of those guards who were on the other shift that you would have taken over from at 7 o'clock in the morning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I replaced Zoran Ergarac, Julije Cindric and Sinisa Popovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am sorry, I thought that you said they were on your shift from 7.00 in the morning to 7.00 in the evening?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were coming, we often switched. My shift was in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just so that it is clear, can I go back to this? What I asked originally were the names of those guards on your shift from 7.00 in the morning to 7.00 in the evening. If you have taken over from Zoran Ergarac, he would be on the night time shift, would he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give me the names then of those guards who were on the night time shift, the shift that you took over from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember exactly, who were coming, but they were coming, the guards, from the environs of Omarska and Prijedor, some locals whom I did not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Zoran Ergarac, was he then on that night time shift rather than your day time shift?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zoran Ergarac was coming to the night shift.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sinisa Popovic, he was on the night shift, was he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It depended, sometimes he would come in the morning, sometimes in the night shift. I am sorry, your Honours, because they were changing, they were coming in the morning and some were coming in the evening to their shifts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your shift had how many guards on it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Four.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The units who came in for that shift from 7.00 to 7.00 was just four guards rather than any more than four guards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So how many guards came in then on your shift?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Four.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you left your post at guard post 4 to go to the white house or other places with Bosko Dragicevic, did you always have a relief guard who took over your position at No. 4?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, from the guard post 1 the guard is watching and he comes to the gate and he watches my guard post.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to give us the names then of who used to stand at guard post 1 on your shift?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot quite recall, but Sinisa Popovic was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At guard post 2 on your shift, who would that have been?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It depended, Zoran Ergarac could be there or -- I am sorry, the guard post 2 ----

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Guard post 3 that you have indicated, who would have been on duty there on your shift?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dragan Maric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us yesterday when you gave us names of the other guards of Zoran Karajica and Milan Cavic that they were Catholics. Can you tell me how you knew that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They went to the Catholic church.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Catholic church where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Towards Kozarac, and the Catholic church is on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also told us that Dusko Tadic visited the camp in a Golf motor car. What I would like you to help me with is whether you can describe anything about that car, what it looked like, its condition. Are you able to help us with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When he came in a car, it was -- then Dusko Tadic drove a white Golf, white but a Golf.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember whether it was a new car or an old car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not brand new.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Any features about that car that you can remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All I remember is that it was white, that it was a white Golf and that he came in it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us yesterday that the day after 26th October, which would have been your first working day at the camp, you saw 10 men being led out of the dom building by Bosko Dragicevic, Zoran Karajica, Milan Cavic and you told us that Dusko Tadic was there as well. At this time were you on your position at guard post 4?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you looking down then towards the dom building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us where you saw Dragicevic, Karajica and Cavic, where they came from before they went to the dom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were in the office which is next to the asphalt. They were there and they came out of the office and crossed the road and entered the camp grounds and then went into the dom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The office that you describe, was that also the Red Cross building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this was a separate place that was known as the office, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see them actually enter the dom building from your position at guard post 4?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To enter the dom building, you go under some arches which were at the front of the building, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean in front of the shop?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps if you could see a photograph that we have of the front of this building? I tender this now as D37, your Honour. Perhaps it could be shown to Mr. Niemann as well? There is a Prosecution Exhibit that I know is a head-on photograph, but I cannot remember the number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, are you now talking about the first occasion when the detainees were taken out from the dom on 26th October?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am talking about the second occasion ----

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: Second occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: --- your Honour, which you may recollect the witness referred to as being the next day when 10 men are concerned. [To the witness]: Do you recognise that photograph there as a photograph of the dom building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, I have tendered it. I offer that now as Exhibit D37.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: D37 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If you could just put it on the screen on the overhead projector? This is a photograph taken from the other end of the road, is it not, of the dom building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This photograph had to be taken from the road leading to Kozarac from Trnopolje, and this is the front of dom that we can see here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were women and children or men held in that building or was it a mix of both of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only men were kept in the dom and women and children were kept in the school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you see the people walk into that building from your position at guard post 4?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, what you told the Court was that the three of them, Dragicevic, Karajica and Cavic, walked into that building. Was Dusko Tadic with them at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dusko Tadic arrived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did he go into that building with them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say he "arrived", what do you mean by that? Where did he go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, we say "arrived" which means that he came in that car and reached his headquarters, the office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he was not down at that part of the camp where the dom building was, he was at his office which you have marked for us on the plan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that he eventually went to Kozarac in his Golf. So how long did he stay at the camp for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember how long he was in the camp exactly, but then he turned and went in his car towards Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when Bosko Dragicevic and the others went into that building, how long did they stay in the dom for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About 15, 10, 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also told us yesterday that along with the three named, Cavic, Karajica, Dragicevic, were also policemen. What were the other policemen called, what were their names?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They are police, civilian police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know any of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dragicevic, Zoran Karajica, Cavic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But were there any other policemen there other than those three?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were policemen who worked in the camp and I was there, Zoran Karajica, Dragan Maric, Sinisa Popovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you misunderstood me. I am talking about this occasion when you describe the 10 men being taken from the dom. Other than the three names that you have given, I wanted to know the names of the other policemen whom you have not told us about who were also with them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember a policeman. I do not know. I did not really know them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you know they were policemen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they used to come in police uniforms and they frequently came, but I did not know their names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any of those with Dragicevic, Karajica and Cavic on this occasion when the 10 men were taken from the dom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Likewise, it was this police but I do not know what their names are. I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the group of policemen took the 10 men from the dom, can you recollect where they took them to, what route they took?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They crossed the road leading to Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then they went where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then they took them to the white house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if we put that plan, D34, back on the overhead projector, could you just trace with that pointer the route they would have taken to get to the white house? Thank you very much, Mr. Bos.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Excuse me, your Honour, may I say something? This map here, it is an excellent job, but as regards the white house, it is slightly different in my time. I can draw the plan and the map and show where the white house is and where they were taken. Perhaps the explanation will be easier then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I will give you a fresh plan here which I tender as D38, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is that ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am using again the Prosecution Exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I think what the witness is saying is that he cannot use that plan even if it is fresh to show where the white house is. That is my understanding. Are you saying, sir, that you cannot use that Exhibit that is before you to point out where the white house is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: So a fresh one I do not think will help him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. If I can ask the witness this question? [To the witness]: I thought you indicated with an X that we see on the plan where the white house was yesterday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it is here, but I could explain it more clearly and draw it more clearly, because I did not draw this map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the position that you have indicated with that X the approximate site of the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If that is the case, can you not then trace the route from the dom that they would have led these 10 prisoners upon to take them to the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is all I am asking you to do, sir, using the plan which is a fresh plan which I am asking to be put in front of you. If you could just indicate, again with the use of an X, where the white house is on this plan and draw the route from the dom to the white house that these 10 prisoners would have walked to get to the white house, using your red biro which is on the desk in front of you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the plan].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you can indicate again with the use of a square the office?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could put that on the screen by your side? So what you have indicated then is the path from the Kozarac road up to the white house, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is when you come out of the dom, you get to the office and it is the road leading towards Kozarac. Then you pass behind the office and then you follow this road and reach the white house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Dusko Tadic at the camp when those three men and the other policemen went into the dom as you saw them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When they left the dom with the 10 men, was Dusko Tadic in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When they moved from the dom and arrived at the white house, how long did that take?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot say exactly, but from the white house to the dom it was about 350 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they walking at ordinary walking pace?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Normal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Dusko Tadic arrive at the camp after they had been to the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Dusko Tadic arrive at the camp before they arrived at the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dusko Tadic came and then -- and then they took out 10 prisoners and Dusko Tadic left off in his car. He turned and went off towards Kozarac and those 10 prisoners were then taken to this white house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are saying before they went into the dom Dusko Tadic had arrived at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as what happened in the white house on that occasion is concerned, you did not hear any gun shots, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were the ages of this group of 10 men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you ever been into the dom yourself where the prisoners were held?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you ever been into those other buildings in front of the dom where there is an office and other rooms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next matter you told us about concerned 5th November 1992, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By this stage you had been working at the camp for over a week, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any new guards that had joined your shift during that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the guards on your shift the same guards at 5th November as they had been in the previous week or so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again on this occasion you describe Dragicevic, Karajica, Cavic and Tadic. You told us that Sinisa Popovic would cover your sentry post, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did that mean that he was going to stand at guard post 4?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. He was at guard post 1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you speak to Sinisa Popovic at all before you went with Bosko Dragicevic to the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Bosko Dragicevic talked to him, not I.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have described over the course of the next two months your involvement in a number of rapes and killings at the white house and elsewhere. Did you talk about these things with the other guards who were on your duty?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Presumably, when people were shot against the post at the white house, those shots could be heard in other parts of the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Silencers were not being used on pistols or anything like that, were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those other guards who were on duty with you, did they not say, "Well, what was that firing about?"

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, if they saw that prisoners were being taken, then they knew that it was to kill the prisoners.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did not then talk with them about any of these things?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have described yourself being involved and Dragan Maric. He was a guard who was on that same day time shift as you, was he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You described him being present at one of these occasions. Were any of the other guards also present at other occasions? By "other guards" I do not mean Karajica, Cavic, Dragicevic or Tadic. I mean any of the other guards who were guards like yourself. Do you know if they were also involved in the same kinds of incidents that you were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Sinisa Popovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember, I cannot exactly remember, but they were working before me, before my time, whether they participated with those other guards whom I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dragan Maric, to my recollection, you described as being involved on one occasion. Was he involved on other occasions, do you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know, but I know that he was -- he started working there before me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ergarac, do you know if he was involved in similar incidents to those that you have described?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am sorry, I cannot remember whether they did anything because they never told me anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, but when you were at guard post 4 at the camp did you see others of them going off with the Dragicevic group to the white house or elsewhere with girls or male prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, as far as I know, the ones that I knew, those were with Dragicevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know why Dragicevic selected you to take part in killings and rapes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe because he got an order from Tadic and because I was the last to come to the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Anything else, anything else that was said to you or gave you any better indication than that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because the first way you are involved is Dragicevic coming up to you and saying had you ever had sex before, was that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And telling him (sic) you could by raping a girl, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that I did not want to do it, that I was not going to obey the order, but I was under threat that I was going to be killed, that I had to do it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The idea from what you have told us is that these girls would be impregnated by Serb men, the idea was to get them pregnant, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Given the conditions at this camp, were these girls in poor physical condition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They were girls who did not receive much food?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were bringing it from their own homes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Presumably, at this time, in November and December 1992, there was not much food for these people to have other than humanitarian aid?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The humanitarian aid was not given them. What they had for food they were bringing from their houses so that they kept it, so that they could have something to subsist on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Presumably, many of them were very thin and under-nourished?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And with illnesses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were involved in, first of all, an attempted rape of one girl where you did not penetrate her and that was the first occasion that you were involved in a sexual offence during this period, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, can you help me that after that first occasion when you are asked to be involved why you were selected later on in the day to be involved in a rape?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because I did not penetrate that girl.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These girls came from where in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am sorry, where did they come from?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I mean, when they were brought and taken to the white house, where had they come from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What route did they take to the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were crossing the road past the office and that they were coming to the white house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, this is in daylight, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the girls were taken from the school, the men taking them had walked into the school, would that be right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to tell us how many female prisoners were in the school during this period, November/December?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not tell exactly, but I know that there were about 1500 of them detained there in the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From what you could see, was the school crowded with these prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not inside the school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From what you could see, were there any male prisoners inside the school building as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During these rapes that took place, you said that the girls were blindfolded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they blindfolded when they left the school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went to the white house and saw the girls, were their blindfolds still on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever not go into the building yourself and take a girl from the building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know why that was not the case, why the other guards, Cavic, Karajica, Dragicevic, did not order you to go into the building with them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because I did not want to go and they did not allow me to go inside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But what would have been the problem here? If you are threatened by them to commit the rape, as you say threatened with guns, there would have been no problem in them just at the end of a barrel of a gun sending you into the school with them to fetch out a girl?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because they knew that there were many prisoners who were watching who was taking them out and who was doing what, and that they could recognise faces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you were a newcomer to this area, no one knew you, did they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These local Muslim people and Croat people kept in this place would not have known you, they would have known the local men, Cavic, Karajica, Dragicevic, Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if they walked into this school building and these were local prisoners from Prijedor, Kozarac, the surrounding villages, all the women in those rooms would have known who they were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they knew because they were from there, because they know Dragicevic and Zoran Karajica and Dusko Tadic, that they lived there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They did not go in wearing masks covering their faces, did they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But if you had gone in there, none of them would have known you or any of your other friends who were refugees, like Sinisa Popovic, Dragan Maric, they would not have known you, would they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they would not because they never saw me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Or, witness, was this the case that you and your friends who were outsiders in this area were going into those rooms and taking girls out for yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What you are doing here is blaming others in the area, other known people, Tadic, Dragicevic, Cavic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not blame them. It is the truth that Dusko Tadic and Dragicevic and Zoran Karajica did go into the school, were taking out girls and were going into the dom and were taking out the elderly men and others, were watching, and Dusko Tadic was giving orders that this had to happen, that these people have to be destroyed, and like those girls who were raped, I also was in fear and fear that I could have been killed if I did not obey what he ordered. That people -- those people are not guilty for having been forced out of their house, houses, and taken into the camp, that those people also want to live. I did not want to do anything against anybody and just wanted to protect myself from not going to the frontlines and getting killed there. Those people have done nothing to me, the people who were in that camp. I came to protect them from others, but Dragicevic and Dusko Tadic and Zoran Karajica forced me to do what I should not have done, that I had to kill, that I had to rape girls. I do not know what reasons. I also have a sister. I feel bad. I know that I am guilty. I was a minor during that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say you volunteered to protect them. You volunteered for work at that camp because you thought you would get paid 300 deutschemarks a month, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was a promise, 300 marks, that would have been the salary but that salary did not happen, but it would protect me from not going to the frontline, but I was not interested in the salary or in doing what I should not have done.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No one came up to and asked you if you wanted a job at a camp. It was one of your friends who took you so that you could get some work?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is not it. I came so that I would have a job, that I would not go to the frontline, not to go as a minor, to work as in the camp, not to touch anybody, not to hurt anybody, and I know that these people have done nothing to me and I had no reason to do something against them. What Dusko Tadic ordered, that these people had to be killed, that the girls had to be raped, that is something else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is what you are saying now, but Bosko Dragicevic did a lot of ordering to you, did he not, not Dusko Tadic who is on trial here but Bosko Dragicevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And he was ordering Bosko Dragicevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that? You do not know that at all. It was Bosko Dragicevic who offered you a job at this camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because he asked Dusko Tadic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us go back to see how you got this job then. Was it one of your friends who was already working at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, but he knew them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who gave you the introduction to Bosko Dragicevic to work at this camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you spoken to anyone else who was working at the camp before you spoke to Bosko Dragicevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I only talked to this (redacted).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he working at the camp as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you talk to (redacted) then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because he knew Dragicevic and he knew Dusko Tadic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So (redacted) introduced you to Dusko Tadic or Bosko Dragicevic so that you could get this job?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you knew already some of the guards who were working there, is that not right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Some of them were refugees from the place that you had come from who had already started work at Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how long they had been working at Trnopolje for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot recall but they came before me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had spoken to them about their work at Trnopolje, how they were spending their time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did you know what Trnopolje was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Or had they spoken to you about Trnopolje and told you that there were easy pickings, getting money off the inmates and also available girls, is that what they told you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, as far as I know, it was only said that there were prisoners there who are Muslims who are interred in the camp and that the guards were needed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But these other people from your area who were working as guards at Trnopolje, were they other young men like you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were some younger ones, but the most were older than I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under 25?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you have told us about these rapes taking place, it seems that the blindfold is taken off in respect of all those girls after they have been raped, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us just look at an example you gave us yesterday of the first time you raped a girl successfully.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am sorry, when they were taken back to the camp their blindfold was taken off.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. You described yesterday that after you had raped her and you started to leave, Milan Cavic also raped her. She was lifted off the mattress and her blindfold removed, and that Dusko Tadic threatened her saying her throat would be slit if she said what happened. You see, when that happens, that blindfold is taken off, she sees Dusko Tadic, does she not? Is that not right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before that blindfold is taken off she has not seen Dusko Tadic at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am sorry, what blind -- the girls who were raped in the basement, their eyes were blindfolded up going to the basement. They were stripped and after the rapes the blindfold would be taken off the girls so they could wipe themselves off. After the rape, she was facing the wall and she dressed and then they took her out of the basement and led her towards the school, to the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us just look then at this blindfold which is to prevent her seeing probably where she is going, would you agree, or who she is with, would you agree?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The girl, her blindfold would be taken off and she would be held under her arms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, and what risk would that give those people who have taken her in a blindfold from the school to that building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When she is taken out of the basement, the girl would be, taken the blindfold off, but during the rape she would not know who raped her.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. As you have told us on all the occasions, as I remember it, that after the rape the blindfold was removed. I think you know what I am getting at, do you not, witness, that there is a risk here that she is going to see those men with that blindfold off?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If she is a local girl, she is going to know Dusko Tadic, Milan Cavic, Bosko Dragicevic and any of the local people, would you agree?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It depends whether she is from the part of Kozarac that she could know Dusan Tadic and the others, then she could recognise his name. If she does not know his name Dusko Tadic, then she can only recognise him by the face of the person who did this to her.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us say that she does not know him then and he is the Camp Commander, as you have told us, she is going to see him around and recognise him at some later stage as being down there when she was raped?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yet this blindfold is taken off?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, what I will put to you again is this. I suggest to you that, in fact, you and your other friends were using these girls for your own purposes, you were not being forced by other people. This is something that you and your friends were up to down in that camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I worked at the camp and I know that Dusko Tadic was in the camp and was the Commander of the camp, and I know that he forced me as a minor to do what I should not, and that what Dusko Tadic also did, raped girls and killed people and gave orders to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You described the occasion when two girls were involved and they were asked to fight each other. Did you find that amusing? Were you laughing at that with the other guards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was not amusing, because I was being forced do what I should not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, in your statement that you gave in Sarajevo on 17th January 1995 that said, "We were all laughing", is that someone writing it down incorrectly, not something you were actually doing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that I was not laughing, that it was hard and it was terrible for me do something as a minor to someone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have told us about having injections.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what those injections were for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Like drugs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you not ever told what they were for, why you were taking injections?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was -- I was feeling weak and sick and when I got my first injection I did not know what it was and later I was feeling different.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have these injections virtually every day when you worked at Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did other guards have the same injections?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see that. I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It seems from what you tell us that it was the nurse who was giving you the injection on most occasions, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nurse Nevenka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Dr. Baja give you injections on fewer occasions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Has anyone ever given you any sort of drug test at any stage to find out what you were being given?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No until -- no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. Where were these injections being put in your body?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The right arm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the arm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the vein.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you had these injections, what sort of effect did they have on you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I felt strong. I had no fear. I had no stage fright.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you not talk about it with your other friends at the camp, as to the fact that you were getting injections every day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, every day when I was coming to work I was getting those injections.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you get them at the start of your shift or at a stage during your shift?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It depended when the doctor came.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What, you would be called away from guard post 4, would you, down to the ambulanta to be told that your treatment was waiting for you, or would they just go up and give you your injection at guard post 4?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I needed those injections. When I received the first one, I continued to receive them and I felt that these injections I needed and the doctor would come into the office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were hooked after the first injection, were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I suggest to you is this, again that you have made this up as part of your excuse for what you were doing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have used age, you are also using drugs as an excuse?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not true. I was receiving drugs and a psychiatrist in the Netherlands had checked that, that I was getting drugs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It sounds like a redaction, but it is also a convenient moment, your Honour, for a break.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Perhaps we can handle the redaction when the transcript is released, but we will keep that in mind. We will stand in recess for 20 minutes. (11.30 a.m.) (Short Adjournment) (11.50 a.m.)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Witness, I would like you to look at this photograph here which I tender as D39, and if you could show it to Mr. Niemann? Do you recognise that photograph, witness, as being taken from the approximate position of guard post 3 that you have identified on the plan for us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, I now offer that to the Court as D39.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 39 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So the Court can see it, can you put it on the overhead projector? You have referred to there being four guard posts. Were there tents in the camp in November and December when you were working there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were all the people then held within the buildings of the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the daytime were the prisoners allowed out of those buildings and allowed within the camp grounds that you have marked on our plan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They only came out to bring some water because they had none in the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But were they allowed to sit on the steps of the school for instance, to -----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: --- sit outside?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Outside they were on the stairs, they came out and got water from other houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you refer to the "other houses", do you mean the houses that were outside the camp in Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Across the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like you to look at this photograph as well which I tender as D40. If you could show it to Mr. Niemann after it has been marked? Do you identify that as being a photograph taken in the road that leads to the railway station and showing the electrical substation which is the area that guard post 1 was positioned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. If that could be put on the monitor so that the Court could see it? The electrical substation is the building in the furthest section of the camp that we see in that photograph, the tower, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the substation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much indeed. Again, at guard post 1 there, was there only one guard standing in that position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I have tendered that as D40. I now offer it to the Court as D40, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No objection, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Defence 40 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That photograph is taken about halfway along the camp perimeter, perhaps even just in front of the dom building. Would you recognise that, the position of where that photograph has been taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the photograph which could have been taken from the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So that it showed the substation and this large shed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And dom is not far from there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is right. I would like to ask you some questions now about your routine at position 4 as a guard. Other than these incidents that you have told us about being involved in killings and rapes, did you just remain at guard post 4 or did you walk around the camp at all during your duties?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We moved around about -- to about midway between guard posts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that just marching along the fence or did you move into the camp nearer to the buildings and see what was happening?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We would walk near the buildings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ever on duty at night time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you walked around the camp in that manner, did you see any other guards other than those positioned at, say, position 1 and guard post 3, who were perhaps working at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For instance, were there any guards near the school or near the ambulanta or the store?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Guard posts, there were only four standing aside and those four guards moved in the direction of one another, close to about halfway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had a rifle, did you, that was part of your duty to carry when you were on duty?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did that rifle remain with you? Did you take it home when you had finished your duty?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to that rifle when you finished your duty?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the end of my shift I would turn it over to the guard who came to replace me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who would that guard generally be who received your rifle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I also took over that rifle and the one that I turned it over to was Zoran Ergarac, Sinisa Popovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any days off at all from your duty or did you have to work seven days of each week?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We worked nonstop around the clock and we worked for seven days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because you referred to asking for a day off from Bosko Dragicevic when you gave evidence yesterday. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you take that day off?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It seemed that he was not refusing you your day off, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you come into work the next day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ask him if you could have a day off on the day after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were working here at the camp during October/November and December, did any of the people leave the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Excuse me, the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any of the prisoners taken away from the camp in buses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember, it did not happen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have told us about receiving these injections during the time that you were on duty. Did you receive those injections in the ambulanta or in the camp office?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Outside the camp, in the office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, did Dr. Baja and nurse Nevenka work from the office or from the ambulanta inside the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were in the office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see them working from the ambulanta?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On your duty, did you ever have any breaks for lunch or for coffee? Did you ever have any meal breaks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We had our lunches at our guard posts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were you fed there? Where did the food come from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We brought it from home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that you were not paid any money, in fact, for working at Trnopolje, so how were you surviving? What did you do for money to buy food?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We had our food which we brought ourselves from home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So where did your food come from home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, we were receiving the first aid from the Red Cross and we had our food which we had brought along.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By that you mean from the place where you came from before you arrived in opstina Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For a number of these rapes and killings that you took part in from 6th November until 25th November, you told the Court that Dusko Tadic was not present, save for the two girls who were concerned with 7th November, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Tadic was -- raped two girls. He was there, and after that in December he raped within the perimeter of the camp when six girls were raped.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it is right to say that you have told us that he was not there at the time of killings and rapes that took place involving you, and you gave us the dates of 9th or 10th November, 15th November, 18th November, that he was not present when those took place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have told us of being involved in the removal of bodies from the area of Trnopolje camp and that they being taken to places (redacted) (redacted). That is right, is it not, you have been involved in that, you told us, on a number of occasions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like you to look at a map now, (redacted)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: (redacted) Can you see those things?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, and you can see (redacted)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. You told us that on 5th November you were involved in a killing in Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have told us that you went to a dump site and these bodies were placed there. What I would like you to do is, if you can using this map, indicate for us on the overhead projector where that dump site would have been where you say those bodies were placed. So, if you could put the map on the overhead projector? Are you able to identify where that dump site for those bodies would have been? Perhaps take the projector off a bit, or move the plan up more so that the bottom is further up. Thank you. Are you able to do that? There is (redacted) (redacted) Are you able to indicate to us -- (redacted) (redacted) -- where the dump site would have been, what route you took?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to remember the route that you took (redacted) on this occasion when you were involved in the killing of these people on 5th November?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was also on the 10th. Excuse me, you think this place which was like a dump site, the earth mover was?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am asking you where you took the three bodies on 5th November which you described as going to a dump site, (redacted)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you identify rather more particularly where it was that you described going to where there was a dump site (redacted) (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Excuse me, where they were digging, where 10 people were killed (redacted) (redacted) -- perhaps that is what you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am asking you about the place you said was a dump site and you described there being skulls, if you can point to us the places, it does not matter on which occasion, where you went where the bodies were buried.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Excuse me, I do not know, according to this map (redacted)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (redacted) we reached the dump site.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. If you can just keep your pointer there, where it would be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Which was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (redacted) where the earth mover was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go to any other site where bodies were also buried and, if so, can you indicate those on the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. This is here, (redacted)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: --- (redacted). This is where people were buried. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (redacted) and that is where these people were buried, those 10 people who had been killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Any other sites that you can indicate to us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One of the sites is (redacted)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When you went to those sites can you remember the names of the guards that you were with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were Zoran Karajica, Cavic, Baltic, Dragicevic and Dusko Tadic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Any other guards that you can name who were with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was Dragan Maric who also knew about this dump site. I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is all I ask.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: One matter, Mr. Kay, you had tendered Defence Exhibits 33, 34 and 36 and they have not been admitted. Do you wish to offer them into evidence at this time?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If I could just remind myself?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I will go through my notes, but I think the Registrar ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. I tendered all of them and offer all of them to the Court.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Do you have them listed, Mr. Bos, as to what they were? 33 was identified as the English statement of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, and he did not adopt it. I cannot offer that actually, your Honour. I do not offer that.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK, then that will not be offered.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is a map, the plan, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That was the one that was modified by the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, I offer that.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 34 -- any objection, Mr. Niemann?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 34 will be admitted. 36?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is a photograph, I offer that.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes, that is the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: No objection. 36 will be admitted. 38 is also a modification of the plan by the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, I offer that, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection to 38, Mr. Niemann?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 38 then will be admitted. Mr. Niemann, is there any redirect?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. Re-examined by MR. NIEMANN

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you were asked some questions about descriptions you had given of Dusko Tadic and especially with respect to the colour of his hair. I ask you to look at this statement of 17th January 1995 which is in your own language and a part of the statement where it is marked with a yellow marker. Can you read it to yourself and then read the section where you have described the colour of the hair of Dusko Tadic? Perhaps this might be shown to the Defence? Witness, if you just look -- I am not tendering this, I do not want to give it a number -- at that section which is marked with the yellow marker and read it, firstly, to yourself? Can you just read out that portion where you describe the colour of the hair of Dusko Tadic, where there is a yellow sticker on the statement? Perhaps before you do that, does your signature appear at the bottom of the statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise that as a statement that you gave at Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I recognise it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you just read out that part where the hair colour is described, please? Take your time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am sorry, should I look at all of it or should I describe him or just the colour of his hair?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just read out the section which makes reference to Dusko Tadic and then lead on to the colour of his hair, the whole sentence. Can you read it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Dusko Tadic, around 40 years of age, born in Kozarac, married, wife" -- here it says "Branka". That is a bit of a problem because I do not know what his wife's name is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Keep reading on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: " ... left Kozarac at the end of 1992, has thick dark hair with some grey, combed upwards and black eyebrows" ----

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: --- "with some receding hair".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Might that be returned, please? Witness, you were asked some questions about the girls being blindfolded and then the blindfolds being taken off. You also gave in your evidence-in-chief evidence about the girls being warned not to tell anybody about what had happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they given this warning before their blindfolds were taken off or after?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, please. Further cross-examined by MR. KAY

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Might I have that statement, please, that Mr. Niemann just used?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: If it is going to be tendered, your Honour, I have a redacted version for that purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I will not tender it. We do not have that version of the statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you look at this statement and look at page 2 and read out the second to last sentence on page 2 where that mark is with the sticky? So if you turn over the page to page 2, the second to last sentence of that paragraph which gives a description, does it not, of Dusko Tadic? Does it say: "Dusko Tadic was sitting at a table"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we were receiving the aid from the International Red Cross"?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you just read out that sentence? Does it say: "Dusko Tadic was sitting at a table. I noticed he was thick set, clean shaven and had short grey-ish hair"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was not grey.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does the statement say it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe they typed it wrong.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does the statement say it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I have that statement back as well, please? Do you remember a list of names at the back of this statement of people who worked at Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sasa Popovic, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Zoran Ergarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Julije Cindric?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dusko Pilipovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am sorry, Filipovic or Pilipovic?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Pilipovic, Filipovic, which one would sound right to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Pilipovic.
