utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he work at Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot say but I know him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you listing him as working in Trnopolje, 25 years old?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He is an acquaintance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the 5th Kozarac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am sorry, I am sorry, that one -- they are known to me, but I -- I did not see them and I did not know they worked at the camp, but those were the ones who were the refugees from my side and maybe they were part of the 5th Kozarac Brigade who were at Brcko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you say in the statement that you met him at the camp? If you want to see the words, have a look at this page here, that you met him at the camp.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just read the passage about Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Dusko Pilipovic, 25 years old, born in Bosanski Bojna, resident of Kozarac, worked as a farmer on his father's farm before the war". Describe him?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. Do you just say that you met him at the camp in this statement and that he was in the 5th Kozarac Brigade in Brcko since the summer of 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember. I do not remember that he was at the camp, but I know that he was in the 5th Kozarac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dragan Ceran, was he at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I only knew him like this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Milorad Oljaca, was he at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I know the name because they were from my region and that some of them went to school with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Rade Ceran, was he at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dragan Maric, was he at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Slobodan Mitrovic was he at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sinisa Popovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Zoran Babic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am sorry ----

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: --- I know all these names, but I cannot recall whether they all worked at the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Here it is in your own language.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am sorry, your Honours, I was only asked whether I knew people, whom I knew and where I knew them from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this statement here in your own language you will see the paragraph beginning "Zoran Babic", does it not say that you met him at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sinisa Popovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Zoran Babic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does it say: "Son of Djuro, about 20 years old"?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I will object to any further reading of that statement, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: OK. But does it say in the last sentence, if you look at the last -- I accept that, your Honour -- sentence: "I met him at the camp"? You can see it in your own language there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it does not say that I met him at the camp. Maybe it says that I found him in the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Pero Zoric, does the last sentence say that you met him at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Pero Zoric was with me in Kalinovik and he was in the first motorized guard Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does it not say ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that it says that I found him in Trnopolje camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does it not say: "I met him at Trnopolje camp" in your own language, this statement that you signed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was a mistake for Pero Zoric. He was in the Kalinovik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain why you said you met him at Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe they typed it wrong.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. Pero Repac, can you see the paragraph dealing with him? It is the last sentence I am interested in. Can you see it in your own language on that page signed by you, that you met him at Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nevenko Dosen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Dosen".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you meet him at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mladen Stevic, did you meet him at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that one was in the 5th Kozarac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Milan Ergarac, did you meet him in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Zoran Karajica you have told us about. Zeljko Karajica you have told us about. Bosko Dragicevic you have told us about. Milan Oljaca, did you meet him in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That man was in the 5th Kozara Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see in this statement that you said that you met him at the camp? Have a look. It is in your own language. I have actually got it here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not have it here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see the paragraph of Milan Oljaca in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see the last sentence, that you met him at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Early '93.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were not working at the camp then in 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here it says I found him in 1993, in the early 1993, in the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (redacted).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you meet him at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dusko Selak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you meet him at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Miodrag Trivun, did you meet him at the camp? Trivun Miodrag? If you would like to look at this? Did you meet him at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does the last sentence say you did?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It says that mid February of '93 was drafted into 5th Kozarac Brigade of Prijedor and the frontline and then -- I am sorry, it is where it says the camp, that is maybe they added while typing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It does say, does it not, that you met him at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "I found him in the camp", yes, it says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you been making up people that you have met at this camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, these people, these are the people whom I knew, and I am sorry if they added things while typing that they were in the camp, but those people were in the 5th Kozara Brigade on the frontline. I knew all these people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who would have been making up things in your statement whilst typing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe they changed while they were typing, the Bosnian side, maybe they said that they were in the camp rather than in the 5th Kozara Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you being told to provide names of people in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Whom I knew?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Were you being told to give any names?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They said to give the names of people whom I knew and where I knew them from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next name, Stojan Draskovic, did you meet him in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew him. It says that I met him at the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, had you met him at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, with these -- if I met them in the camp, I only knew them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But how does it come to be in this statement that you were saying that you met this person at the camp when you are telling us you did not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am sorry, maybe they -- they made a mistake in typing on the Bosnian side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next name, (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know him. He did not work at the camp. He was with me in the International Red Cross where it was distributed. I knew him, I know him very well. He also knows Dusko Tadic. He was not at the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just look at what you have signed to here. It says, does it not, in the last sentence that you met him at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "I found him at the camp".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doing what at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not find him at the camp and nor was he at the camp, this man, but he was where the aid of the International Red Cross was distributed, where he introduced me to Bosko Dragicevic and Dusko Tadic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had this statement read back to you, did you not, by the authorities in Sarajevo and you signed each and every page?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I signed the pages that, where I gave the names of people that I knew.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just have a look at the pages. Every single page of that document from page 1 contains your signature at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This was an interview conducted in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was typed in my own language and then they were typing it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, and you were just making up names of people whom you had seen at Trnopolje, were you not? You have put down people here saying they were at Trnopolje who were not there at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know the people who were not in the Trnopolje camp, and people who -- I also know the people who worked at the Trnopolje camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Here you are saying now that you did not find these people at the camp or you did not meet them at the camp, and you have given all their names?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, I do not want to cut you have off, but you have asked and it has been answered several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am conscious of that.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The witness says, at least, that he was asked to give the names of people he knows.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: He gave them. On the statement, for some of them, it says they were found in the camp and he disputes that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I understand your point, but I think you need to move on to another area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am much obliged. [To the witness]: Let us look at that name after (redacted), is it Miroslav Beronja? Do you say you met him at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you meet him at the camp? Did you meet Miroslav Beronja at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You need to answer. Did you meet him at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I only know him, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So, what has happened here in this statement? Has someone made it up for you saying that you met him there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I tell you, maybe the Bosnian side typed it wrongly. I apologise. I know people who were not there. I know that they are the refugees from my region whom I know, who are in the 5th Kozara Brigade, and some were in the camp as I gave that earlier who was in the camp working.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, the next name, Predrag Vajgic, did you meet him in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Well, perhaps you would like to look at the second to last sentence. Does it say: "I heard from Zoran Ergarac and Sinisa Popovic that Vajgic committed many rapes and murders. He used to arrive at the camp drunk, take people out to rape them and kill them in the white house. I met him at the camp"? Can you see those sentences dealing with Zoran Ergarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Zoran Popovic, Sinisa Popovic, I heard that Vajgic had committed a large number of murders and rapes, that he used to come to the camp at night and drank."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the rest.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "He took out women and girls so as to rape them and kill them in the white house. He is at present at Brcko frontline. I found him in the camp.” After midnight that Predrag Vajgic, I do not know whether he came to the camp at night time. I did not work then nor do I know that he did all this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, did you just say that you found him in the camp at night time?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to that. He did not say that at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Quite right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Excuse me, I did not work nights.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You found him at the camp ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Excuse me, this Vajgic I know him, but I did not find him at night in the camp because I did not work nights.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Does the last sentence of that statement about Vajgic say that you met him at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have said in this statement that you did discuss with Zoran and Popovic then what this man was doing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Popovic?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you find him at the camp, Vajgic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Predrag Vajgic?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That one was not in the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear from Ergarac and Popovic that he had committed many rapes and murders?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They talked about that man, but I do not know whether he did that and whether that was true. I did not see him with my own eyes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they talk about him committing murders and rapes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They talked about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I thought you did not discuss with Ergarac and the other guards you knew what had been happening?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In my time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you go on, Ranko Mitrovic who is on this page. (Handed) Ranko Mitrovic, did you meet him at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Excuse me, your Honour, I know it says that all of them were in the camp, but they are men of the 5th Kozara Brigade who went to the front. Perhaps this was in typing that the Bosnian side put it wrongly and perhaps they added they were at the camp. I only know these people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, this list gives Bosko Dragicevic, Milan Cavic, they were not all at the front with the 5th Kozara Brigade, were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were not. They were in the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Zeljko Karajica was not in the 5th Kozara Brigade or Zoran Karajica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were in the camp. They were not in the 5th Kozara Brigade. They were not on the frontline. They were in the camp who committed and performed murders and rapes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact this document, which is in your own language, says before this list that: "Among the policemen and guards who were there at the time I know the following ... " If you go back to the beginning of the list, if you look at page 23 here. (Handed). I have put a sticker at the start of the sentence. What does that sentence say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It says: "Apart from me, there were about 20 guards working at the Trnopolje camp, 15 military police."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does the rest of the paragraph say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That: "The others were civilian policemen who came from the village of Petrov Gaj and Omarska."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the next sentence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "These civilian police used to come to the camp at night together with guards, with guard, and a smaller number of military police and among the guards" [INTERPRETER: We are very sorry, but those cases are all wrong. It is simply incomprehensible].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think it is not being read properly by you, Witness. Are you changing the language in the statement in any way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Among the guards there were also military police. I know the following ... "

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then you go on to give the list, do you not, of names?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were taking the names of people I knew and people who worked in the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. So that it is clearly put I will say this to you. Have you just given those names of people that you have made up allegations about them in Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: People I do know and some who worked in the camp and people who were on the positions of the 5th Kozara Brigade, this is what the Bosnian side requested, what people I knew and what people worked at the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the next page do you say, "Sasa Popovic committed a number of murders and rapes before I arrived at the camp"? Do you see the paragraph beginning, "Sasa Popovic", the last sentence? "Dragan Maric told me that Sasa Popovic had committed a number of murders and rapes before I had arrived at the camp"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because he worked at the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that true, that Dragan Maric told you that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Zoran Ergarac, did you say you heard from Sinisa Popovic that Ergarac committed a number of rapes and murders in Trnopolje camp before I arrived"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object. Could we be told what is true, whether the rapes were committed or whether the question was asked?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I will overrule your objection. Was it true?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was it true?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: If you had objected, Mr. Niemann, that this whole line of testimony was beyond redirect we would have recessed 25 minutes ago, because you only asked him in the statement what was the colour of his hair. Go ahead, Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was it true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour that is all I ask. May I say I had not seen this document before, we do not have it, which is why it came in.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. Well, it was clearly beyond redirect but that is OK. We have very liberal rules. Mr. Niemann, is there any re-redirect?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, your Honour, but I ask that the statement be returned.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. I just have one question while the statement is being returned. Mr. Usher, would you get the statement so we can just move along. Examined by the Court.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Sir, you worked in a guard post, as I understand it, is that correct, while you were at Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There were four guard posts as you have described them, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You worked from 7, was it 7 a.m. to 7 p.m.?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So would there have been another shift coming behind you to work from 7 p.m. to 7 a.m. in the guard post?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there other guards at the camp, though, who did not work in guard posts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any other guards who just guarded the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because otherwise there would only be eight guards at Trnopolje camp, and certainly there were more than eight guards, were there not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were more, but I did not know them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These other guards who you did not know, they were performing other duties, I gather, other than assigned to a guard post?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were they doing or do you not know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know what they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, you did not have any meetings with the other guards, any kind of regular meetings with guards, who did not work in guard posts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who would you take your orders from on a daily basis?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To commit murders and rape?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, to perform your duties in the guard post? Did you have ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Bosko Dragicevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is the person whom you testified got you the job, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have testified that you believe Mr. Tadic was the Commander of Trnopolje camp. Why do you believe that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was the Commander because he issued orders to kill the people and to rape girls.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But he never gave you any orders on a daily basis, did he, tell you which guard post to go to, that kind of thing, did he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Bosko Dragicevic was his deputy. Tadic was only asked whether something could be done to an inmate or a girl and that that people were not to be let free.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is why you believe that he was Bosko's superior?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann, do you have additional questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, do you have additional questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Just arising out of what you have been saying, Zoran Karajica and Cavic, they were not one of the eight guards, were they, in the guard post?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they would come to the camp. With Bosko Dragicevic they came and did those things, committed those killings and rapes and be present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They were not working full time in the camp then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann, do you have additional questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Regarding the transcript for L, since this is in closed session, we have asked as our usual procedure that the transcripts be reviewed and any corrections you may have you get those to us as quickly as possible. If you can get the corrections to us by Friday at 5 p.m. -- I understand you are leaving, Mr. Wladimiroff -- that would be helpful, and then they can be gotten to the Witnesses Unit for their review before we release the transcript. Is there any objection to this witness being permanently excused?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to keep him still under command of the Court, so to speak, not to release him.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I have no objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Sir, you are free to leave. You are still under the control of this Tribunal, in that you may be recalled as a witness. So you should make yourself available. We will stand in recess for an hour and a half for lunch. (1.24 p.m.) (Luncheon Adjournment) (2.55 p.m.) PRIVATE (Open session)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We are now in open session continuing. Mr. Niemann, would you call your next witness or is it Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. Thank you. The next witness will be very brief and will be in English. The next witness is Grant McIntosh junior. MR. GRANT THOMAS McINTOSH JUNIOR, called.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Sir, would you please take the oath that has been handed to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. (The witness was sworn)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Fine. Thank you. You may be seated. Examined by MR. TIEGER

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Can you state your full name, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Grant Thomas McIntosh, junior.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. McIntosh, you are presently an investigator for the Office of the Prosecutor of the International Criminal Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long have you worked in that position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am seconded from my government to the Tribunal. I have been here since June 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you previously worked as a criminal investigator?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For how many years?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 28th of this month, I will be starting my 19th year.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With what agency were you previously working?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The United States Naval, Criminal Investigative Service.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that capacity, were you a sworn law enforcement officer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, a civilian special agent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. McIntosh, did you recently complete an investigative mission to Bosnia and elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were the dates of that mission?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 4th August through 11th August.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the course of that mission were you in opstina Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While in Prijedor, did you visit and photograph part of the site which was the former detention camp at Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Specifically, did you photograph the area of the dom or hall in a building housing a store and a medical facility?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I have this photograph marked as Exhibit 315 for identification, please? Mr. McIntosh, do you recognise this photo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What it depicts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is a photograph of a part of the structure of the dom that housed the store and the medical facilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender this photograph for admission and ask that it be placed on the overhead projector.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, objection your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 315 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: First of all, Mr. McIntosh, how do you know that there was a store and a medical facility there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Upon arrival at the front of the building on the street side, which is located right here, there was a store that was opening and functioning as a store at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were you able to determine there was a medical facility of some sort in that area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: By looking through this middle window, I could see that there was some sort of a medical office with medical supplies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You took this picture from the parking lot of the dom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From what part of the parking lot, where would you be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Approximately in front of the main entrances to the dom with the large hall area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What date was this photograph taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 9 August at about 4.30 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This photograph, as we are looking at this photograph, we are looking in what direction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Towards the town of Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would your back at the time this photograph was taken, therefore, be to the Trnopolje railroad station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you also take photographs from the position of the two windows to the left side of the building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do those photographs also depict this parking lot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, they do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are there landmarks or identifying features in this photograph, Exhibit 315, which would help us identify portions of the parking lot in the other photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, there are several marks, what I would call divots in the asphalt parking lot, one here, one here, and there is like an oil mark here. There is also a basketball backboard that is depicted in the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I have this composite photograph, montage photograph, marked as Exhibit 316 for identification? Mr. McIntosh, do you recognise this montage of photographs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it is a bracketed photograph, a series of three photographs that are put together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do they depict the area of the dom parking lot and the surrounding area, including a portion of the hall building itself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I tender 316 for admission, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 316 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: May that be placed on the overhead projector as well? First of all, Mr. McIntosh, can you point out, identify, those points of reference or identifying features in the parking lot which you indicated earlier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. The first one would be this divot here in the asphalt parking lot that I mentioned. This would be the second one. This would be the oil that is on the ground and here is the basketball hoop with backboard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was this photograph or bracketed photographs taken? Where were you standing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went to the first window that was shown on the first photograph to the left and put my back to the window as if I was, like, looking out the window, and would take a series of photographs starting from the left to the right with my shoulder, bracket the photograph, second photograph to third photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to get inside the building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, sir, we were not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you point out for us the dom or hall building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That would be -- the entrance to the dom hall building would be here, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: OK. Your Honour, may I have this next series of bracketed photographs marked as 317 for identification? Mr. McIntosh, do you recognise these photographs, Exhibit 317, as being a set of four bracketed photographs that you took with your back to the second window?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I recognise them and I believe actually there are five.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender 317 for admission.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 317 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Once again, Mr. McIntosh, can you point out the points of reference in the parking lot which indicate where we are relative to the picture that shows the medical supply and store building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again, the first two in would be the divot in the asphalt here, No. 1, No. 2 would be here, the oil spot, and again the basketball backboard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I could have 315 placed briefly on the Elmo? Just to clarify, sir, 317, the series of five photographs, was taken with your back to which window? Can you point it out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The centre window here, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The previous series of bracketed photographers was taken from where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This window here, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we have 317 back on the Elmo? I am sorry. Mr. McIntosh, during your approximately 20 years of investigative experience, have you had many occasions to take photographs of various scenes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Although the camera, obviously, captures the details of objects seen, does it sometimes fail to accurately reflect the dimensions and distances as perceived by the human eye?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your experience, what kind of effect can be seen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The type and size of the lenses that you might utilise, maybe the angles from which a photograph is shot, can make the image or the objects in a photograph appear either closer or further away than what they actually are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did that effect occur here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The objects, everything here, appears to be further in distance then when you are actually standing there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were at the scene, at this area, last week, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you estimate for us the distance from the wall at which you were standing, the window at which you were standing, to the end of the parking lot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would estimate approximately 60 feet or so which I understand is about 18.5 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In terms of this courtroom, what would a rough approximation be, if you can make it, of the distance of that parking lot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Probably from inside this doorway over here to my right to probably inside the other doorway over here to my left. Approximately the same, maybe a little bit further.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If one were to be at approximately the area of the entrance to the dom and then move perhaps three or four metres in the direction of the corner of the parking lot seen at the left of the picture, approximately how far would that be from the hall at which you were standing where the window was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would have to say approximately 45, 40 to 45 feet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. McIntosh, during your time in Prijedor did you also visit the Omarska mine, the former site of the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you take photographs there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I have these two photographs marked as Exhibits 318A and B?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: May I ask one question, Mr. McIntosh, to understand your testimony? Regarding then Exhibit 317, if one were to move how many feet from the front of the dom over to the left towards the basketball court, and then how many feet would it then be from the wall of the medical centre to that place? Tell me that again, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I understand the original question, if you -- approximately nine feet or so from where the start of the dom, at the entrance to the dom, out into the parking lot towards ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I am sorry, you say nine feet what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If one was to move approximately nine feet or so, nine to 10 feet, from the entrance towards this far corner, it is what -- and then I would say it was approximately 40 to 45 feet, without knowing exactly where someone was standing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then 40 to 45 feet from where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the wall, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the wall of the medical centre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right where I am standing taking the photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is where you were. You were taking the photograph from the wall of the medical centre, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if you move nine feet or so from the entrance of the dom going towards the basketball, you then become 40 to 45 feet from the wall? I do not understand how that is possible. Maybe I am missing ----

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If I could really clarify that, your Honour?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: --- because I thought it was 60 feet normally from the wall to the entrance to the dom.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: To the end of the parking lot, I think the question was.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Tell me again because I do not have the dimensions correctly. Speak more loudly for me. I guess, we have been in closed session and I think maybe I am used to it being closer.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I apologise for the confusion, your Honour. First of all, Mr. McIntosh, understanding that these are approximations, standing from the wall of the medical facility to the end of the parking lot, is that a distance that you approximated as about 60 feet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would say approximately 60 feet, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then the second question was -- we can also see the entrance to the dom in this picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then again the question was, if one were to move approximately three to four metres, and again roughly approximating the distance, in the direction of the corner of the parking lot, as you pointed out before, then you would estimate that distance, based on your presence there last week, as being approximately 40 to 45 feet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, sir, recognising that the parking lot went a little bit further beyond than the doors, about 15 feet.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Where is the entrance to the parking lot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The entrance would be right through here, ma'am, right through here. But the parking lot would extend to the other side of these columns.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. McIntosh, do you have those photographs from Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what 318A and B depict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The photographs were taken outside of the large hangar, demper garage area, at the entrance to the garage doors.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These are the series of large garage doors on the other side of the entrance to the hangar building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender 318A and B for admission.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 318A and B will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If B may be placed by its side? Mr. McIntosh, does the grate shown in 318A extend for the full length of that side of the hangar building, as far as you recall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I could see, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 318B just shows a close up of that grate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, the photograph downward.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Incidentally, Mr. McIntosh, when you visited the Omarska camp, before you visited the Omarska camp, had you seen photographs and videos of camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you actually visited the camp, did you notice anything about the distorting effect you spoke of earlier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first thing, I was really surprised to see that the white house was as close to the back of the demper garage area as it actually was. From the photographs that I had seen before, I had always envisioned it to be much further away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any other portion of the camp which struck you in the same way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The pista between the cafeteria of the building and the demper building, to me, in photographs it looked much larger than when I was standing there and observing it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we could return just a moment to 316, please? Just to clarify, Mr. McIntosh, we see the columns that indicate from where we see the portion of the entry area to the dom, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, right here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The parking lot extends a little bit further than the entrance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then when you add the nine or so feet, I guess nine to 12 feet, whatever, would be, in the question I asked you, you would estimate the distance then would be approximately 45 feet from the wall of the medical building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Coming out from the doors to the distance that you asked, I would say then about 40 to 45 feet, depending upon where the individual or the person would be standing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is all I have, your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay? Cross-examined by MR. KAY

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Just to assist me, did you use a 35 millimetre lens on your camera?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I did -- excuse me, a 35 millimetre camera. It was a 35 to 80 zoom lens.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you use the zoom lens on any of these photographs you have shown us of the parking lot (as it has been described) in front of the dom building at Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, but I could not tell you the exact -- what exactly it was, what measurement it would have been, from the 50 -- between the 35 to 80. I was just framing the picture.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand. So you moved it up from 35 millimetres to somewhere in between 35 to 80?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was somewhere in between, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. In relation to these distances from the wall of the ambulanta building, did you measure those?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, sir, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So these are sites that you are giving by eye and judgment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In this particular case, I did not measure because I was not tasked to, sir. I was just tasked to take a photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Nothing further.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection to this witness being -- you have a question? Examined by the Court

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Witness, you have talked about distortion that photography can produce. Would you have a look at the model in front of you of Omarska? Perhaps you can stand up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have a good look at it. Does it accurately represent, for instance, the position of the white house and also the size of the pista?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would say that it accurately represents that. Again, it just appears to me that the white house seems a little further back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that you think it does accurately represent?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it does accurately represent. I am trying to look over it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, your Honour, nothing further.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to Mr. McIntosh being permanently excused?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, there is not, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Sir, you are permanently excused. You are free to leave. Thank you very much for coming. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you. The Prosecution calls Mr. Robert Reid. MR. ROBERT REID, called.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. (The witness was sworn) Examined by MISS HOLLIS

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Would you please state your full name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My full name is Robert William Reid, spelt R-E-I-D.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your current position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am an investigative team leader at the Office of the Prosecutor, the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long have you held this position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Since 6th June 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What are your duties in that position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My principal duties are to lead direct and co-ordinate all investigations which are allocated to the team by the chief of investigations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For what organisation did you work before taking your current position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was with the New South Wales police service in Australia and I am currently on leave without pay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you work for that organisation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In December of this year it will be 21 years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What types of investigative work have you been involved in in the past?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Since about 1978, I have been involved in criminal investigation and that covers the whole sphere of criminal investigation from murder, sexual assaults down to simple stealings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What prior experience have you had with war crimes investigations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In July of 1987, I was seconded from the New South Wales police to the Federal Attorney General's office where I was attached to the special investigations unit which was investigating allegations that persons had entered Australia at the conclusion of World War II, who had committed serious crimes during the conflict of World War II in the period 1941 to 1945. I remained in that position until 1991 when I returned back to the New South Wales police. There was a period, however, between 1991 and 1992 where I worked at the committal proceedings and trial of a person who had been charged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Reid, what duties have you performed in relation to the Office of the Prosecutor investigation of the accused in this case, Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have been the lead investigator in relation to the investigation of the accused. In addition to that, I am the investigator in relation to the investigations relating to opstina Prijedor and Bosanska Krajina, the area of Bosanska Krajina in the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Reid has asked to be able to use a short aide memoire during his testimony. I have provided that to the Defence and asked them if they have any objection to that. I would ask that he be allowed to use the aide memoire.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. Wladimiroff?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You may use it, Mr. Reid.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Mr. Reid, in your capacity as lead investigator for this case, were you the team leader of a mission that went to opstina Prijedor in February/March 1996?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were other OTP personnel part of that mission as well as other investigative personnel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did personnel from the team visit various locations in opstina Prijedor, including the sites of the former detention camps at Omarska, Keraterm and Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that mission did the team photograph and video tape various locations in opstina Prijedor, including the former detention camps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the team also seize evidence from various locations in opstina Prijedor, including from the former detention camps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Reid, I would first like to ask you some questions about evidence that has already been admitted in this case. At my request, did you review Prosecution Exhibits 232, 239A and B, 240, 248, 250A, 251, 256, 257, 258, 259, 260, 261, 262, 263, 266, 267, 270, 272A and B, 273A, 279, 312 and 314 which were photographs of various locations at the former Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When were those photographs taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were taken on the mission to opstina Prijedor between 19th February and 4th March 1996.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At my request, did you review Prosecution Exhibit 229 which is a video of various locations at the former Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was that video taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was taken on the mission again between 19th February and 4th March 1996.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At my request, did you review Prosecution Exhibit 130A, floor plans of the large hangar building at Ormaska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who prepared that Exhibit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That Exhibit was prepared by Miss Kate Pearce, the analyst on the team.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From what source or sources was that Exhibit prepared?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were taken from a set of plans that were seized at the former Omarska mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These were seized during your team's mission to opstina Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, between 19th February and 4th March 1996.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were at the Ormaska camp, did you enter the buildings there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this large hangar building on the model before you, were you able to determine how well sound carries in that building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Sound travelled quite easily within that large hangar building. In fact, we carried out a number of tests while we were in there, where I went to particular rooms and areas of that large hangar building and another member of the team simulated the calling of names. The room, one particular room that I went to was room 15 which was on the first level. I also did it from the internal stairway. I also did it from a room which has been called the electrical workshop which is on the ground floor. The noise travelled quite easily and I could hear quite distinctly what was being said. In addition to that, while I was working in the area upstairs I could often hear people talking, laughing. I could hear noises and doors closing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were at the camp, did you take measurements at various locations in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I took two particular sets of measurements. I measured the pista area, or what has been referred to as the pista area, which is the area between the large hangar building and the administration building, and I took a measurement from the corner of the hangar building closest to the pista across to the front door of the white house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The measurements that you took on the pista, what were the measurements?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the wall of the administration building -- perhaps I can indicate where I took it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you would, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From approximately this point here on the model across to this wall of the large hangar building was 32 metres and 37 centimetres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were at the camp, were there concrete flower pots of a sort in that pista area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were. There was a set of concrete flower boxes which ran along the pista in this direction and ran along in this direction. I measured between those two points and the distance was 28 metres and 78 centimetres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you measured from the inside of the flower pots on one side to the inside of the pots across the pista?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What other measurements did you take?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I took one other measurement. Perhaps I could walk around to indicate that? I took a measurement from this corner across to the front door of the white house, and that distance was 37 centimetres -- 36 metres, I am sorry, and 75 centimetres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You pointed, I believe, to the corner of the hangar building that is closest to the restaurant?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, across to the front door of the white house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Reid, if you could come around again, please? You have mentioned some room numbers, and if you could show us what room numbers you are talking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, if I can remove the .....

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please. First of all, Mr. Reid, you mentioned a room 15. Was that a room number that was marked on the door?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in the camp there were two room 15s. Room 15, if I can distinguish as B14, and there was also another room 15 which was marked in texta colour on the door which was B7, which also incorporated B8, B23 and B7 and a corridor B7 as well. That was marked in texta colour, and that room was at the top of the external staircase. Stencilled on that door in white was the room 7. The room that I did the test in relation to the noise within the hangar was at B14 -- if I can just take the top here off -- the internal stairwell which is marked A15 on this model and the room, the electrical workshop, which is marked A17 on this model.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you Mr. Reid. At my request, did you also review Prosecution Exhibits 201, 227 and 228 which are photographs of various locations at the former Keraterm detention camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When were those photographs taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were taken on the mission to Prijedor between 19th February and 4th March 1996.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At my request, did you review Prosecution Exhibits 204, 205, 277A, 301, 302, 303, 304, 308 and 310 which are photographs of various locations at Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When were those photographs taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were taken on the mission as well between 19th February and 4th March 1996.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At my request, did you review Prosecution Exhibits 203, 296 and 307 which are video tapes of various locations at Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When were those video tapes taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were again taken between 19th February and 4th March 1996 on the mission to Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were at Trnopolje or while you were in opstina Prijedor, did you measure the distance from Kozarac to the entry of what was the former Trnopolje detention camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was that distance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The distance from the main Prijedor/Banja Luka highway to the entrance of what was in the summer of 1992 the entrance to the Trnopolje camp was 5.2 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we could have Prosecution Exhibit 280, please, provided to the witness? Mr. Reid, if you could take a moment to orient yourself on that plan and then if it could be placed on the overhead projector?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The road that I took the measurement from is this road Prijedor/Banja Luka which is depicted in the red colour, along here, Kozarusa, and then down and I came along this yellow road leading from Kozarac, down to approximately this area here where the entrance to the camp is. That is the Trnopolje/Kozarac road. That was 5.2 kilometre distance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the 5.2 kilometres was from the intersection of the Prijedor/Banja Luka road following this yellow route down to the entry to the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At my request, did you also review Prosecution Exhibits 197, 198, 199, 200, 202, 204, 205, 210, 212, 222A, B and C, 224, 237A, 299 and 300 which are photographs of various locations in the town of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When were those photographs taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were taken on the mission to opstina Prijedor between 19th February and 4th March 1996.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At my request, did you review Prosecution Exhibits 107 and 195, video tapes of various locations in the town of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When were those video tapes taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again on the mission to opstina Prijedor, between 19th February and 4th March 1996.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At my request, did you review Prosecution Exhibit 238A and B, photographs of Benkovac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When were those photographs taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Between 19th February and 4th March 1996 on the mission to opstina Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At my request, did you also review Prosecution Exhibit 284A through E which are photographs of a location in the village of Sivci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When were those photographers taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again they were taken on the mission to opstina Prijedor between 19th February and 4th March 1996.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At my request, did you also review Prosecution Exhibit 283, a video tape of various locations at the village of Sivci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was that video tape taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were taken between 19th -- it was taken between 19th February and 4th March 1996.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At my request, did you review the photographs contained on Prosecution Exhibit 287 as well as Prosecution Exhibits 288, 289, 290, 291, 293 and 295 which are photographs of various location in the hamlet of Jaskici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When were those photographs taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Between 19th February and 4th March 1996.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were those taken by members of your team during your mission into the opstina Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In regard to seized documents, I would like you to review the following documents. If this document could be marked the next Prosecution Exhibit which will be 319A and B? If I could have copies, please? The original will be in the Serbo-Croatian language and B will be an English translation. If that could be provided to the witness, please? Mr. Reid, what is that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a document that was seized in the Omarska iron ore mine between 19th February and 4th March, and it is entitled "A break-down of diesel consumption from 23 May 1992 until 20 October 1992".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could put the English translation on the overhead projector, please? What organisations does this document show as receiving fuel from the Omarska mine during the period in question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There are a number of organisations that are receiving diesel fuel but, in particular, the Territorial Defence in Omarska, the JNA, the police and the municipal Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the document in the Serbo-Croatian is that how the JNA is annotated as "JNA"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would offer Prosecution Exhibit 319A and B.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 319A and B will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this next Exhibit is a composite Exhibit which will be 320A through L.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Before you leave this 319B, can the witness explain what the matter is in the bottom half, I suppose, of the plan, the KSs and what follows below them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The KS, I take to mean Krizni Stab which is Crisis Staff. As to the figures below that and the reason for it being there, I am unable to explain, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Mr. Reid, what are these documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These are documents that were seized again at the Omarska iron ore mine between 19th February and 4th March 1996, and they are reports on the quantity of fuel received by individual vehicles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you would start with A, please, and tell us the dates on each of those documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the date on document A is 2nd June 1992. Document B is 4th June 1992. Document C is 6th June 1992. Document D is 7th June 1992. Document E is 9th June 1992. Document F is 10th June 1992. Document G is 11th June 1992. Document H is 12th June 1992. Document I is 15th June 1992. Document J is 16th June 1992. Document K is 18th July 1992. Document L, it is 19 and 20 July 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 19 and 20 July?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am sorry?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 19 and 20 July?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Each of those documents, A through L, is there a Serbo-Croatian and then an English translation for each of those?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there one vehicle that appears on all of those reports?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What vehicle is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a TAM truck registered No. PD54546.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do those documents also appear to list the driver or the person who is putting fuel into those documents (sic) ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: --- or into those vehicles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those vehicles, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do the reports show tanks receiving fuel at Ormaska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they do.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I would tender Prosecution Exhibit 320A through L.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 320A through L will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were on your mission in opstina Prijedor, did you also request materials and documents from the Chief of Police of opstina Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this request pursuant to an order from a Judge of this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Chief of Police give you any of the requested materials or documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the chief of Police allow any team members to review the materials or documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the name of the Chief of Police with whom you were dealing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Simo Drljaca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As part of your duties in relation to this case, were you provided with documents sent to the Office of the Prosecutor by Germany authorities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What documents did you receive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 29th December 1994 I received 10 volumes of folders, and they contained the, if you like, German investigation in relation to the accused. On 26th January 1995, I received volumes 11 through to 14 of what I referred to as "seized" documents which were documents taken from the home of the accused on the day of his arrest in Munich.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You indicated that you received binders 1 through 10. Did you receive a record of interview of the accused that was done by German authorities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did. That was contained within volume 5.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time that the Office of the Prosecutor received these materials, how were they provided to the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were provided through the Embassy of the Federal Republic of Germany here in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once the Office of the Prosecutor received the seized documents, what was done with those documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
