utterances.text: The documents or the binders 11 through to 14 were registered in the normal fashion. They were photocopied and the originals of the seized documents were placed in the vault.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The German record of interview that you received, was it the original record ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: --- of interview?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it is a copy of the record of interview.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I could have this Exhibit marked as Prosecution Exhibit 321A and B, 321A being the German version and 321B being the English translation. What is this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the first document that I am looking at, 321A, is the German record of interview in the German language that was conducted between German authorities and the accused on 11th, 12th and 13th October 1994 in Munich.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you look at that Exhibit, is there a gap in the page numbering in that Exhibit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there is. The page numbering commences (and I am speaking about the paginated numbers in the top right hand corner) at 3 and it goes through to the number 12, I think it is, it is number 12, and then it begins again at paginated page 30. The reason for this was that at the conclusion of the first day of the interview, 11th October 1994, an annexure was placed at the back of that day's interview which became paginated pages in these volumes, 13 to 29. The next day's interview, 12th October, commences at paginated page 30 and goes through to the conclusion of the interview at page 51.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I would offer Prosecution Exhibit 321A and B.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is no objection. We just need to check the translation from the German and if we could hold that as a proviso?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Subject to that opportunity, Exhibit 321A and B will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If I could have this, please, marked Prosecution Exhibit 322A and B? Mr. Reid, if you will look at this document and on A there are numbers 13 through 22?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is the document that was inserted as an annexure at the end of the first day when Mr. Tadic was interviewed in Munich, and it is a letter addressed to the Consulate of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia in Munich. From 23, paginated page 23, to paginated page 29 was the German translation of this document.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution offers Exhibit 322A and B.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 322A and B will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If we could have this Exhibit marked as Prosecution Exhibit 323A and B? This has a Dutch or, excuse me, a German stamp of 1.12.24, for the Defence's assistance. Mr. Reid, what is this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a blank form from Republika Srpska, Prijedor municipality, Municipal Secretariat for Town Planning, Housing and Public Utility Services and Property Law, and it is a blank form of a decision. But there is nothing filled in in the areas where there should be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We received this Exhibit from whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was received from the German authorities on 26th January 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From where was this Exhibit obtained?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document was taken from the home of the accused when it was searched on his arrest in Munich on 12th February 1994.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution offers Exhibit 323A and B.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 323A and B will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If this Exhibit could please be marked Prosecution Exhibit 324? For the Defence's purposes, this is 1.12.47. Mr. Reid, what is this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is again a document that was found at the home of the accused on the day that he was arrested in Munich. It is a piece of blank paper and it is a round seal with the inscription "Republika Srpska, local commune, Srpski, Kozarac, Prijedor municipality".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From whom did we receive this Exhibit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the German authorities on 26th January 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did they obtain this Exhibit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the home of the accused on the day of his arrest when the house was searched.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: We offer Prosecution Exhibit 324.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 324 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If this could be marked as Prosecution Exhibit 325 for identification? This is 1.12.34. Mr. Reid, what are these documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a document, a number of pieces of paper, with the heading "Serb Democratic Party", underneath that "Prijedor", underneath that "No." On the bottom right-hand corner is the seal of the Serb Democratic Party.

utterances.text: May I ask that this Exhibit be marked Prosecution Exhibit 328 for identification? [To the witness]: What is this Exhibit?

utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.text: Is that one document or is there an A or B?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That is fine. 328 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If I could have this Exhibit marked, please, Prosecution Exhibit 329A and B for identification, B being the English translation? This is document 1.7.2. [To the witness]: What is this Exhibit?

utterances.text: This document is the employment book of the accused Dusko Tadic.

utterances.text: Does that employment book indicate that it is a duplicate book?

utterances.text: Yes. In the English translation the word "duplicate" is there, but on the first page you can see quite clearly at the top of the page "duplicate".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that book that you have before you, 329A, is the word "duplicate" written in ink on that book?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is in blue ink.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to that book, by whom was the accused employed in October 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: October of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: By the Republika Srpska, municipality Prijedor, Local Commune, Srpski Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From whom did the Office of the Prosecutor receive that Exhibit?

utterances.text: I tender Prosecution Exhibit 329A and B.

utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 329A and B will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If this could be marked Prosecution Exhibit 330A and B, B being the English translation? This is document 1.12.73. Mr. Reid, what is this document?

utterances.text: This document is dated 30th December 1980 and it is the registration of a karate club in Kozarac by the name of "Borac", B-O-R-A-C.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From whom did the Prosecution receive this document?

utterances.text: From the German authorities.

utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.text: If this document, this Exhibit, could be marked Prosecution Exhibit 331A and B? [To the witness]: What is that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this document is a confirmation that Dusko Tadic is a coach in the karate club, Borac, in Kozarac and the confirmation is issued on his request for enrollment to the senior coaching school in Zagreb. It is dated 15th March 1981.

utterances.text: From whom did the Prosecution receive that document?

utterances.text: Yes, we received 333A and B from the German authorities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did they obtain the document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the home of the accused on the day of his arrest in Munich.

utterances.text: 334A and B for identification is 1.12.65. What is this document, Mr. Reid?

utterances.text: In this document, according to the document, what two organs does it indicate as the working organs of the commune?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We received that document from whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the German authorities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did they obtain the document?

utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.text: This is a decision that was taken at the meeting of the local board of the Kozarac SDS appointing Dusko (Ostoja) Tadic as the Party representative for the Kozarac area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.text: This is a document which was sent to the SDS Municipal Committee in Prijedor and its suggestions re. the names -- the change of names of institutions, streets and squares in the area of the Serb Kozarac Local Commune. It is dated 21 March 1993.

utterances.text: From the Republika Srspka, Prijedor municipality, Local Commune, Serb Kozarac.

utterances.text: From whom did the Prosecution receive this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS

utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a document sent by Dusko Tadic, son of Ostoja, Kozarac, to the Municipal Secretariat for City Planning, Housing, Utilities and Real Estate in Prijedor, and the subject is the change of location of business premises. It is dated Prijedor, 5.8.1992, and it is signed "Dusko Tadic".

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 338A and B will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If this could be marked Prosecution Exhibit 339A and B? This is document 1.12.41. Part B of that Exhibit is the English translation. What is this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a document which lists seven business premises with their address, the previous owner and the floor space. It is date 29th December 1992, Prijedor. It appears to be a surveyor's report as it is an on site investigation conducted by a surveyor, but the name is unclear.

utterances.text: Are one of the premises listed there the Okej cafe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, No. 2, there is the Okej cafe bar at Ulica Edvarda Kardelja Street, previously owned by Sead Dracic, floor space approximately 50 square metres.

utterances.text: Where did the Prosecution obtain this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the German authorities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did they obtain it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the home of the accused on the day of his arrest.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 339A and B will be admitted.

utterances.text: Your Honour, do you intend to take a break or do you want to continue through?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: No, we will take a recess. I was just looking. We started at 10 to 3. We will stand in recess for 20 minutes. (4.30 p.m.) (Short Adjournment) (4.50 p.m.)

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.text: What are the premises that are being leased?

utterances.text: The premises are in Prijedor, Edvarda Kardelja Street, consisting of 50 square metres, consisting of one room.

utterances.text: Does the agreement indicate the rent amount per square metre for those premises?

utterances.text: This is a document that is dated 8.8.1993 entitled "My Work Report in 1990-1993".

utterances.text: From whom is this or by whom is this document written or prepared?

utterances.text: From the home of the accused on the day of his arrest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, at the time the record book was offered into evidence and admitted we did not have a complete translation of all of the portions of the book. The Prosecution has now prepared such a complete translation and I have it here available to assist the Court, if you wish it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: So we will have 345 and then 340A and B?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you want to make it a separate Exhibit or if it would assist you as part of the Defence Exhibit, however you want to handle it.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You can make it Exhibit ----

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Defence D8.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I recall that the Defence offered it to Colonel ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: This is simply to assist the Court.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Good. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you wish me to mark it as a separate Exhibit?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: However you wish.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Right, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You are doing well with this stack here! Just keep going.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If the Defence has no objection, perhaps we can make it Defence Exhibit 8A so that we keep it together.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: A good idea. We tender that!

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: It will be a joint Exhibit -- well, it will be 8A, is that it, Defence 8A?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. We have one to be marked as 8A and we have three copies. We have previously provided the Defence with a copy. Mr. Reid, at my request did you also review the following Exhibits: Prosecution Exhibit 146, Prosecution Exhibit 147, 148, 149, 150, 151, 152, 153, 154, 155, and 156?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From whom did the Prosecution receive those Exhibits?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the German authorities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did the German authorities obtain those Exhibits?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the home of the accused on the day of his arrest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Reid, in the course of your investigation into the events that occurred in opstina Prijedor, did you determine that the word "pista" was often used as a reference for a concrete area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. In fact, some witnesses who were detained in Keraterm camp referred to a concrete area within that camp as a "pista" as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Reid, you had mentioned earlier that when you were at the former Omarska detention centre you went into the buildings there including the large hangar. When you were in the large hangar did you see any types of hooks or pulleys hanging from the ceiling of that building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I could have these two photographs marked as Prosecution Exhibits 345 and 346, and if a copy could be given to the Defence. There are three additional copies. It does not matter which is which. Sir, do you recognise what is depicted on those photographs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is within the large hangar building, the ground floor workshop area. In Exhibit 345 in the top centre is the type of pulley that I have described, that is being described, and in Exhibit 346 in the top centre is a similar pulley.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If these could be put on the overhead projector, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you point to the pulley that you were talking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is the pulley here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That pulley, where does it descend from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not sure if it descends completely from the roof or from a bar or from a rafter, iron girder from the ceiling.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this photograph taken during the mission, the OTP mission to opstina Prijedor in the spring of this year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could put Prosecution Exhibit 346 on the overhead. If you could point to the ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The pulley is this area here [The witness indicated].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again where does that descend from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the ceiling or an iron girder.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These are two of the pulley-type structures you found in that building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I offer Prosecution Exhibits 345 and 346 for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 345 and 346 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Mr. Reid, I have asked you questions about documents that were seized from various locations in opstina Prijedor, including the former detention camps. Were all of these documents seized pursuant to the Court order that you took with you on this mission?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No further questions of this witness, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I have no cross-examination, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to Mr. Reid being permanently excused?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour -- no, your Honour. I had in mind he would be around.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I know what you mean. Mr. Reid, you are ----

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we do request he be subject to recall.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Reid, you are excused. However, you should continue to make yourself available for you may be recalled.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you for coming.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honours, that is the evidence of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay or Mr. Wladimiroff?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Defence, as you know, will be filing a motion which the Court will receive on Wednesday of next week concerning submissions of no case to answer in relation to certain of the charges. The Court is to go into recess now until 10th September, as we understand it, and the Defence are to visit the area that we are concerned with in this court next week. We will be returning in various stages after that visit. The Defence case, as we see it, will probably be opening then on 10th September after the Court has made observations or rulings in relation to the submissions. We will be inviting the Court to receive oral argument, such as the Court requires it, in relation to those motions of no case.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. You then expect you will be filing the written motion to dismiss some or all of the counts by August 21st, is that Wednesday of next week?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The Prosecution then will have 14 days to respond to that motion. Then we would like to hear oral arguments on the motion on September 10th at 10 a.m. That was the date we were to return from the three-week recess that has been requested.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Fine. That resolves that matter. A few other matters we would like to discuss. Yesterday afternoon we discussed the Defence's motion for protective measures, and heard argument in closed session. We expect that we will issue the decision with respect to that motion by tomorrow at 5 p.m., so that you will have that to take with you. Earlier I mentioned that the parties should endeavour to submit their comments on the transcript of witness L by 5 p.m. tomorrow. Once again, if we have the comments from the parties by 5 p.m. tomorrow, then the Witness Unit will be able fully to look at it and the transcript, perhaps, will be released then by Tuesday of next week. Mr. Wladimiroff, you agreed that you will notify the Trial Chamber by August 28th regarding the two-week period that you would need for video conferencing.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes, I will, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I think that is all that we have regarding preliminary matters. The Trial Chamber wants the parties to know that we will be available, the Judges will be available during this recess here in The Hague. Should you need to communicate with the Trial Chamber, contact the Registry and the Registry will be in touch with us. Are there other matters we need to consider at this time, Mr. Niemann?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: There is one matter I wish to enquire of the Defence through your Honours, and that is whether the Defence will be providing the Prosecution and the Court, or the Prosecution, with a prior list of witnesses indicating the intended order of witnesses as they propose to call them.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We had not intended doing that. We have supplied the names of the alibi witnesses and expert witnesses that we intended to call. We had not intended to supply a list of names of all our witnesses. It does not seem to be something within the Rules.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann, are you referring to the expert witnesses and the alibi witnesses? Are you asking for an order, an order in which the Defence would call the witnesses, or are you asking for a list of all of the witnesses?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, what we are asking is whether or not a list of the witnesses that the Defence intend to call, whether or not they will be supplied in advance of them calling the witnesses. So, yes, I am referring to all of the witnesses, but whether we will be provided with that. If I might just go on, your Honour, it does touch upon important matters because we have issues such as video conferencing. We do not know when those witnesses will be called. We have been given no indication for it. Particularly with respect to the placement of expert witnesses, we do not know where they are going to be placed. In our submission, it would considerably assist the smooth running of the proceedings if we were to be provided with these in advance of them being called.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, we will be as helpful as possible. May I say we do not know our own order yet because we do not know when the video link is going to be in operation. We are hopeful that the live witnesses can be dealt with first, but they are still ongoing discussions between the Defence and Witness Unit as to how precisely that is to take place, whether the witnesses are to be brought over in dribs and drabs, batches or as a job lot. So we do not know our order yet, but we will certainly advise the Prosecution when we are to call our expert witnesses, because they will obviously want to have their own experts present and available to listen to the testimony. We are still working on this, your Honour, and we are unable to provide them any indication at this stage, not least because we do not yet know when the availability of certain witnesses is going to be possible.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That is why I was trying to ask the Prosecution whether he was focusing on expert witnesses or alibi witnesses or both of them, plus all of the other witnesses. It seems to me that he is requesting a list of the order for all witnesses. With respect to the alibi and the expert witnesses, it seems to me you can give, certainly as to expert witnesses, the order in which you intend to call them. As to the alibi witnesses, you should be able to give them an order at some point. The question is when. When you return back from visiting the Former Yugoslavia it seems to me you will then be in a good position to know what your order will be. As far as the video conferencing is concerned, I thought you had indicated that you would be calling your live witnesses first when we returned in September?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The persons, that is, who will come to The Hague. Are you in a position at this time to give the order of those witnesses and then perhaps in the next week or two weeks you will know better about the remaining alibi witnesses?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We will certainly know better after our visit that is pending. The only reason why I hesitate over the video conferencing is I know the Court advised us it was only for a two-week period. It is going a fixed two-week period.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That may fall into the middle of live witness time.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Why do you not provide the list to the Prosecutor of the order of the expert witnesses and alibi witnesses whom you intend to call. As the Prosecution has changed their order, you may change your order.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We have received five, six different Prosecution lists, and they have worked with you and changed the order. So we are certainly willing to handle your list in the same manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am obliged.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: So if you can provide them with an order, a list of expert witnesses and alibi witnesses and the order in which you intend to call them as best you can estimate at this time, understanding that there will be a change, by the Friday before -- when would you want them Mr. Niemann?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The Friday before the commencement of the case.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The Friday then before we commence. That would then be September 6th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Also by then we will be in touch, the Registry will be in touch with you and I am sure we will have the video conferencing, still keeping our fingers crossed that we will have that in place. I am sure that by the Friday before we will have established the two-week period. Things should be working pretty smoothly by then. But then I am optimistic by nature!

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I think one has to be given the problems we have faced over the last few months. We are aiming to start with policy witnesses, your Honour, and I am sure that will assist the Prosecution rather in the same way that they did.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Are these expert witnesses?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. So then you will provide them with that list by the Friday before, but just of expert and alibi witnesses. We will consider a request that you may wish to make for all witnesses at a later time. Are there other matters that we need to consider at this time?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Nothing, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. Then we will adjourn until Tuesday, September 10th at 10 a.m. (5.20 p.m.) (The court adjourned until Tuesday, 10th September 1996).
